strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple simulation benchmarks (RoboCasa, SIMPLER-WidowX, LIBERO) and real-world robotic tasks with consistent improvements (28% in-distribution, 35% out-of-distribution, 168% in low-data regime)
Practical verifier-free approach that leverages model's internal properties without requiring external training or modules, addressing key limitations of prior verifier-based methods
Thorough ablation studies (Table 5) systematically analyzing inference strategy, number of candidates, masking variants, joint training, temperature, and aggregation strategy
Well-motivated problem identification: clear articulation of how greedy decoding becomes a bottleneck for high-precision manipulation tasks and why external verifiers have generalization issues
Efficiency-conscious design with single-prefill deployment strategy achieving 45% latency reduction while maintaining performance
Joint training strategy to make models aware of condition-masking distributions is sensible and shows measurable improvements
Clear presentation with good figures and explanations of the approach
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core mechanism (using KL divergence as confidence metric) is adapted from recent LLM work (Kang et al., 2025); the contribution is primarily application of existing techniques to VLAs rather than fundamental methodological advance

Significant hyperparameter sensitivity and dataset-specific tuning: requires different masking variants for different benchmarks (state-masking for RoboCasa vs. text-masking for LIBERO), different architectures require different aggregation strategies, and extensive hyperparameter search over 4 dimensions needed per-dataset

Heuristic design choices lack rigorous justification: (1) temperature regularization τ=4.0 justified only as 'regularizing concentration' without principled analysis; (2) using first 5 tokens for aggregation justified post-hoc by speculation about tokenizer structure; (3) no principled justification for why masking conditions specifically creates good uncertainty estimates

Modest improvements in several settings: SIMPLER-WidowX shows only 3.4 point improvement (46.9→50.3%), LIBERO-Spatial actually decreases with π0-FAST (97.4→97.2%), and real-world 'Plate to Basket' shows only 4.2 point gain, suggesting results are highly task-dependent

Missing direct empirical comparisons with verifier-based methods (Nakamoto et al., 2024; Kwok et al., 2025): while theoretical drawbacks are discussed, lack of side-by-side comparison weakens claims about superiority

Lack of theoretical justification: no principled analysis of when/why KL divergence from masked distributions should work as confidence metric, under what conditions the approach should succeed/fail, or what distribution properties enable this approach

Real-world evaluation limited in scope: only 60 demonstrations per task, 4 objects, 4 tasks, small sample sizes (16-24 trials), and no confidence intervals or statistical significance tests; no comparison with other test-time scaling methods on real robot

Token aggregation findings (Table 5f) raise concerns about method brittleness: aggregation strategy heavily impacts performance (sum worst, first-5 best), suggesting sensitivity to tokenization details and potential transferability issues across architectures

Joint training overhead underexplored: while joint training improves results, computational cost of training with 4x data variants not discussed; unclear if this negates claimed advantage over verifier-free approaches
Missing ablations: no analysis of single-prefill deployment's effect on action quality, no cross-dataset generalization testing, limited sensitivity analysis for hyperparameter changes

strengths: Addresses a genuine and important problem in VLAs: improving precision of action selection without external verifiers

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple simulation benchmarks (RoboCasa, SIMPLER-WidowX, LIBERO, CALVIN), real-world robot experiments, and multiple model architectures (π0-FAST, OpenVLA, MiniVLA)
Consistent practical improvements: 28% gain on real-world in-distribution tasks, 35% on OOD tasks, 168% relative improvement on low-data regime
Extensive ablation studies thoroughly investigating design choices (inference strategy, candidates, masking variants, joint training, temperature, aggregation)
Practical efficiency consideration with single-prefill deployment achieving 45% latency reduction
Well-motivated departure from verifier-based approaches with clear explanation of their limitations (extra training, poor generalization)
Thorough reproducibility documentation with detailed implementation details and hyperparameter specifications
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: adapts existing self-certainty measures from LLMs (Kang et al., 2025) to VLAs using condition-masking instead of uniform distribution—somewhat incremental contribution

Severe hyperparameter sensitivity contradicts 'verifier-free' claim: requires per-dataset tuning of temperature τ, number of candidates N, masking variant, and regularization temperature via grid search; no principled guidance for new domains

Critical tokenizer-dependence: aggregation strategy varies by model (first 5 tokens for π0-FAST, first 1 for SIMPLER-WidowX, average for OpenVLA) with dramatic performance variation (26.1%-31.0%), suggesting brittleness

Incomplete theoretical justification: why condition-masking vs. other perturbations? Why is τ=4.0 optimal? Appendix E proves entropy increases with temperature but doesn't explain the principled choice
Performance inconsistencies on already-strong baselines: LIBERO-Spatial shows degradation (97.4%→97.2%), LIBERO-Goal (95.6%→94.5%), suggesting method may hurt when base model is already good
Weak baseline comparisons: RoboMonkey comparison relegated to appendix on single benchmark; no direct comparison with value function approaches (Nakamoto et al., 2024) mentioned in introduction
Best results require joint training with condition dropout, adding complexity and contradicting 'verifier-free' positioning; no results without joint training on all benchmarks
Limited real-world evaluation: single robot platform, pick-and-place tasks only, small OOD set (2 tasks); would benefit from task diversity
Insufficient analysis of failure modes and when/why the method underperforms; Figure 4 failures show method introduces unnecessary stochasticity but limited discussion
Reproducibility challenges: extensive per-dataset hyperparameter search, unclear how hyperparameter ranges were determined, no code release mentioned

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple simulation environments (RoboCasa, SIMPLER-WidowX, LIBERO) and real-world robotic tasks with strong consistent improvements (168% relative gain on RoboCasa with 30 demos, 28% on real-world tasks)
Practical verifier-free approach that requires no external training or model loading, with efficient single-prefill deployment strategy reducing latency by 45% compared to vanilla sampling
Demonstrates generalization across multiple VLA architectures (π0-FAST, OpenVLA, MiniVLA) and model scales, showing broad applicability
Thorough ablation studies (Table 5) systematically analyzing inference strategies, number of candidates, masking variants, joint training, temperature, and aggregation strategies
Clear problem motivation addressing limitations of existing verifier-based approaches (requiring additional training and failing to generalize to unseen conditions)
Good reproducibility with detailed implementation details, hyperparameter ranges, and training configurations provided in appendices
Formal theoretical analysis (Appendix E) justifying temperature scaling of reference distribution
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: adapting self-certainty measures from LLMs to VLAs is incremental, and the core idea of sampling multiple candidates with a confidence metric is straightforward

Condition-masking design lacks rigorous justification: claim that masking 'approximates failure modes' is intuitive but not validated; no theoretical explanation for why KL(masked ∥ predicted) correlates with action quality; missing comparison to alternative reference distributions

Significant dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning required: different masking variants optimal for different datasets (text vs. state), requiring grid search over multiple hyperparameters (τ, temperature, variant); this contradicts the verifier-free narrative

Ad-hoc aggregation strategy: optimal token truncation differs across benchmarks (first 5 for RoboCasa, first 1 for SIMPLER-WidowX), with post-hoc explanations about tokenizer structure; lacks principled approach
Incomplete failure analysis: limited discussion of when/why method fails; shows performance regression on LIBERO-Spatial (97.4→97.2); no analysis of behavior when base model already performs well

Joint training adds complexity: requires modifying training procedure with condition dropout, dataset-specific dropout ratios, creating two separate training pipelines; unclear if necessary beyond providing marginal gains
Incomplete comparison with related work: RoboMonkey only evaluated on SIMPLER-WidowX where it achieves 50.7% vs. 50.3%; missing comparisons on other benchmarks to establish clear advantages
Latency overhead understated: Table 10 shows 1.17× latency increase for N=4 even with single-prefill; may be prohibitive for real-time applications; wall-clock time analysis missing

Limited analysis supporting core claim: paper claims VLAs produce 'overly concentrated' distributions but provides limited empirical evidence (entropy measurements, distribution visualizations); doesn't explain why this fundamental issue isn't addressed at source

Limited scope and generalization: all experiments focus on pick-and-place manipulation tasks; unclear how method scales to longer sequences or other robotic task types; single robot used for real-world experiments
